Connect - TV camera interface TV CAMERA INPUT The interface is an NTSC (National Television Standard Comittee)-format composite video type. Two pins of the MQS connector are dedicated to this interface. These are connected to the video signal and reference (cable and shield). TV CAMERA POWER SUPPLY Connect supplies a dedicated power source to the TV camera. The power stage is software-managed so that it can be enabled or disabled as required. TV camera menu No dedicated TV camera management menu is present. Data Interface Function Connect is designed to manage a DCE-type external hardware device (e.g. Computer, printer, ...) The configuration normally used for computers, terminals, printers etc. is defined a DTE (Data Terminal Equipment) configuration. The configuration normally used for modems is defined a DCE (Data Communications Equipment) configuration. These different configurations define the type of signal that each device expects at each pin. Any device may be configured as a DTE or DCE. Connect acts as a DCE, the external device (typically a computer) acts as a DTE A lead with a direct pin-to-pin connection is used as a connection device for this configuration. Maximum transmission speed is as specified for the GSM Phone module, i.e. 9.6 kbps. A serial line consisting of a lead with a direct pin-to-pin connection is used to connect the Connect system to the external device. No dedicated connector is required. The pin-out is described in the paragraph on the pin-out. Priority. The serial interface used allows the system to detect data transmission/reception on the channel and thus establish access priority levels to the GSM transmission module. Data interface priorities for Connect functions are described below. TARGAsys SERVICES Emergency calls (in automatic mode) and/or Connect key depression suspend all activities in progress on the serial line to make the GSM module available for the selected purpose. The following message is displayed: Serial Connection Interrupted. All data exchanged during the interrupted communication session on the serial line are lost. At the end of the emergency call or activated service, the previously active communication session on the serial line is not automatically resumed. PHONE FUNCTION When the Data Interface function is active, the following conditions are determined: Phone menu locked Input caller block Outgoing caller block The data interface cannot be activated when a phone call is in progress. NAVIGATION FUNCTION When the Data Interface function is active, the Navigation Function can be activated. Serial line data transmission may be slower if the Navivation function is active. RADIO / CD / MP3 PLAYER FUNCTIONS These functions are independent of the Data Interface function. Actiation, deactivation and use of the Data Interface The DEFAULT status upon activation of Connect with key-ON or key-OFF is: Data communication on RS 232 line INACTIVE. Note that engine start-up with a serial line GSM data communication session active causes the line to drop and loss of transmitted data. Conversely, engine shut-down does not affect the serial line GSM data communication session. After engine shut-down, the Connect system remains active for 20 minutes unless the left encoder is pressed (immediate shut-down) or the GSM communication carries on. If the GSM communication carries on to the end of the 20 minute period, a second 20 minute period will automatically start. Note that extended serial line GSM data communication sessions (and also long phone calls) can drain the vehicle battery. ACTIVATION/DEACIVATION PROCEDURE Select the MAIN menu and press the encoder to display the options (See "Fleet management" paragraph). Select Setup (See "Fleet management" paragraph). Press ESC to go back to the previous screen in all cases The field to the left of the "Serial" option (1) indicates current status: Serial "Inactive" = serial communication not possible Serial "Active" = serial communication operational To change status (from "Active" to "Inactive" and back), select "Serial". Status changes automatically. If the "Serial = Active" is selected, the data can be transmitted using the application selected on the comuter. If the option " Serial = Inactive" option is selected, Connect automatically restores normal service modes and full phone operation in particular. If GSM field intensity is insufficient or the SIM card is not inserted or invalid, the "Serial" item cannot be selected. Status cannot be changed and therefore remains "Inactive". In this case, no communication session can be opened with data transmission/reception via the serial line. 1 - Serial FAILURE TO DEACTIVATE SERIAL COMMUNICATION If the option "Serial = Inactive" option is not selected at the end of data Transmission/Reception via computer, the procedures described in the Priority paragraph continue to apply. In particular, if an attempt is made to access the Telephone menu or if the key is pressed to call the last number dialled, the following message will appear: SERIAL COMMUNICATION ACTIVE: TELEPHONE NOT AVAILABLE. SETTING COMPUTER TO BE INTERFACED The computer interfaced with the Connect system must have: serial port set for a transmission speed of 9600 bps. A modem installed. If the modem is correctly installed, all applications that require a telematic link with external databases/servers may be used. Speed alarm function Operating principle The Speed Alarm function issues an acoustic alarm and a visual alarm when vehicle speed exceeds a preset threshold "Vlim" (Speed limit). The speed alarm and acoustic alarm function can be activated/deactivated from a dedicated menu. The acoustic alarm takes the form of a set of tones. The visual alarm takes the form of a screen message (1) "Attention: speed limit exceeded" that is displayed for 3s after the threshold has been exceeded. This visual alarm takes priority over every other display. The alarm contains symbol (2) containing the set value. Exceeding of Vlim triggers the acoustic and visual signals. The acoustic signal remains active for a time established by the acoustic signal screen and the screen signal remains active for up to 3 s. The signals are deactivated for V < Vlim-5 regardless of time elapsed The user enters a numerical speed limit value by turning the encoder. The numbers change in steps = 5. Speed range [30-250]km/h, or [20-155] mph The measurement unit applied to input numbers is as specified in the Setup menu in the "Distance Measurement" field (km or Miles). If the speed alarm is deactivated (Alarm = inactive) and the speed limit is changed (e.g. from 130 to 190), it will activate automatically. When the measurement units are changed from km to miles and viceversa, the number representing the speed threshold (Limit key) remains valid but takes the new measurement unit into account. The set values are active only after confirming with the "OK" key.. Settings Display the MAIN page and press the right encoder to display the items "Store item" and "Setup", Then select "Setup". Select the option "Speed alarm" (1) on the "Setting and Control Selection" page. 1 - Speed alarm Access the "Speed alarm" page To change alarm status from Activated to Deactivated, select the Alarm option (1) and press the right encoder. To enter a speed limit, select the option "Limit" (2), press the right encoder and turn to alter the figure displayed. The measurement unit is as set in the Setup menu under Distance Measurement. To Activate or Deactivate the acoustic alarm (Buzzer), select the option "Buzzer" (3) and press the right encoder. Status will change automatically. At the end, highlight OK and pres the right encoder to confirm the settings. 1 - Alarm 2 - Limit 3 - Buzzer 4 - OK

SPECIFICATIONS he overtaking sensor is a device located inside the driver's door mirror. This surveys the blind spot on the driver's side to help ensure safer overtaking manoeuvres. he device monitors the area at the side of the vehicle and notifies the driver of the presence of overtaking vehicles. In particular, the device is able to indicate approaching vehicles in the lane alongside the lane in which the vehicle on which the device is installed is driving. The vehicle fitted with the sensor can detect vehicles up to 20 m away. Notification is by means of a lighted signal that turns into a sound signal when the turn signal is on (left turn signal for left-hand drive vehicles, right for right-hand drive cars). Notification begins when the approaching vehicle is still visible in the door mirror. The TV camera used as an active sensor includes a darkened area that delimits the image acquisition field to reduce possible glare. The device is intended as a complement to the use of the current rear view mirror and is not intended to be used in place of the rear view mirror. Because the system is based on vision, the function may be fully or partly lost when environmental conditions reduce visibility to less than 20 m (e.g. thick fog, sandstorms). The device consists of: a TV camera inside the door mirror that is positioned to ensure scanning of areas that are otherwise hard to see, a special control unit in the door compartment that can analyse the input signal and transmit a visual signal (led) and acoustic signal (buzzer), a driver interface (positioned on the driver's side door inner panel) that includes: an indicator led and an acoustic signal (buzzer). 1 - TV camera 2 - Indicator LED and buzzer The system notifies the driver of potential danger, e.g. if an overtaking vehicle draws level, by turning on a led. If the turn signals are activated (to indicate an intention to overtake) under conditions of potential danger , the control unit activates the buzzer to warn the driver that the manoeuvre is potentially dangerous. e system is enabled only at speeds higher than 30 km/h. At speeds betwen 30 and 80 km/h, the scanned area is directly proportional to speed. The scanned area reaches its maximum extent at speeds higher than 80 km/h. SYSTEM OPERATION The device uses a B/W TV camera as a sensor and not to display the image directly on a monitor. Instead, the image is analysed by a special electronic control unit to identify and indicate the presence of overtaking vehicles even before they enter the door mirror blind spot. The presence of approaching vehicles is indicated until they enter the driver's direct line of vision. 1 - Half of front view area 2 - Overtaking sensor coverage area 3 - Side coverage area of one left mirror 4 - Vehicle travelling in the second lane that cannot be seen through the door mirror but can be detected by the overtaking sensor The system works on the principle of analysing the optical flux generated by the TV camera during vehicle motion. Everything within the scene recorded by the TV camera displays apparent motion in the direction of the vanishing point on the horizon (1), i.e. objects captured by the TV camera move away from the horizon. The presence of an overtaking vehicle is detected by the control unit because the TV camera picks up the image of an object that grows steadily larger (2). The object's presence is communicated by a light signal and an acoustic warning is also sounded if the driver has operated the turn signals. A - Horizon line 1 - Vehicle moving away 2 - Vehicle approaching (overtaking) Area monitored by device The system is enabled only when vehicle speed exceeds 30 km/h The area of analysis is subject to change according to the speed of the vehicle equipped with device. These changes are shown in the following table. Speed of vehicle equipped with device Extent of analysis area V < = 30 Km/h. Device disabled 30 Km/h < V < = 60 Km/h Device operating with analysis area extended to 10 m. 60 Km/h < V < = 90 Km/h Analysis area extent ranging from 10 m to 20 m V > 90 Km/h Analysis area extent = 20 m The extent of the analysis area is modulated in this way to avoid excessive signallling to the driver in the case of low-speed driving. Side light activation allows the system to detect headlamp lights (day and night discrimination). A - Overtaking sensor maximum coverage area Warnings may be issued incorrectly under the following conditions: Left-hand bend taken at speed (not systematically) Speed bumps (particularly if repeated) Shadows of vehicle in the third lane (under specific lighting conditions, when the shadows are projected into the area screened by the device). System self-diagnosis The warning light also acts as a system status indicator (on/off, operating faults). The system is automatically activated when the vehicle is started, and carries out self-diagnosis as follows: BEHAVIOUR UPON START-UP: when the system is working properly, the led comes on for about 2 seconds to inform the user that the initial test has been carried out correctly. if the warning light (led) is faulty, the buzzer emits a series of three pulses lasting about 1 second each; if the sound indicator (buzzer) is faulty or the TV camera is faulty, the led comes on with a constant light; BEHAVIOUR UNDER STEADY-STATE CONDITIONS: The system monitors itself continuously and indicates faults by turning on the led.

SPECIFICATIONS The parking sensor option plays a part in helping parking manoeuvres in tight spaces. The system helps prevent damage to the vehicle (and third parties) by identifying rear obstacles located outside the driver's field of vision. Four ultrasound sensors located in the rear bumper use sonar technology to survey the area behind the vehicle. They send incoming information to a microprocessor control unit that combines the data to establish the presence or absence of potential obstacles. The system alerts the driver to potential danger by emitting an intermittent acoustic signal. The signal rate is inversely proportional to distance from the obstacle (the signal is continuous below 250 mm). The device is automatically activated when reverse is engaged. It can, however, be excluded by a special button.

fuel level gauge with reserve warning light and signal repetition unit; various warning lights (fault, activation etc.); panel lighting, graphics and pointers, with LEDs; LED mileometer lighting even during daylight; Odometer The milometer is the digital electronic type with an LCD (liquid crystal display) with 1 line. The milometer display is illustrated in the diagram When the ignition is turned on (+15) the display is lit up and the milometer provides a reding of the total mileage or the trip mileage in the appropriate unit of measurement - Km or Miles. The button (31 in the diagram) manages both the zeroing function for the trip mileage rading and the selection of the total/trip mileage through the following operating mode: (a) when the total mileage is displayed pressing the button for between 0.1 seconds and 2 seconds produces a switching to the trip mileage when it is released; (b) when the trip mileage is displayed, pressing the button briefly (in other words between 0.1 and 2 seconds) produces a switch to the total mileage when the button is released; pressing the button for a while (between 2 and 5 secs) inolves zeroing the trip mileage displayed. 7 digits with 6 segments are used to display the total and trip mileage The TRIP symbol on the milometer appears when the partial mileage is displayed The trip meter counter returns to display "0.0" when the figure "999.9" is exceeded, whilst when the total mileage counter exceeds 999999 (Km or Miles) it only displays the centre segments of all the digits (in other words 6 horizontal "bars"). Planned maintenance The servicing function lets the user know when the vehicle is ready for service when the distance or time parameters approach the deadline set for the engine and application type. Distance and time parameters definition The parameters used for calculating the services are the distance travelled and time. The distance travelled is calculated using the vehicle speed input with an upper limit of 99999 Km and the time is indicated in days and taken from the clock function. There is a spanner symbol for the servicing function that appears each time the ignition is switched on if the conditions for the service displayed below have been reached. MILEAGE AND TIME REMAINING UNTIL THE SERVICE SPANNER KEY FOR THE FIRST 5 SECONDS AFTER THE IGNITION IS TURNED ON SPANNER KEY FOR 5 SECONDS AFTER THE IGNITION IS TURNED ON Km > 2000 TIME > 30 DAYS ON OFF Km > 2000 TIME < 30 DAYS ON ON 0 < Km < 2000 TIME = ELAPSED ON ON Km = 0 TEMPO = ELAPSED FLASHING FLASHING FOR THE DURATION OF THE DISPLAY, THEN ON CONSTANTLY The calculation and the comparison with the values set is made when the ignition is turned on and if the spanner symbol does not appear within 5 seconds then it will not appear during the journey. The milometer LCD becomes an interface with the user for zeroing the servicing. Zeroing servicing parameters The servicing time and the distance can be zeroed after each service and the spanner symbol switched off. The procedure is to keep the button (31) pressed with the ignition on and the vehicle stationary for more than 8 secs; the new parameters are memorized in this way and the total mileage is diplayed. The servicing parameters are initialized during the only zeroing permitted within 200 Km for the total milometer. When the battery is first connected the distance travelled is the one indicated by the total milometer and the time is 0 days. Subsequent disconnecting/reconecting of the battery do not cause the distance calculated earlier or the time in days to be lost. Engine oil level sensor When the ignition is turned on the milometer displays the engine oil level for five seconds. This level is read by measuring the voltage at the sensor located located in the engine oil sump. The difference in power measured allows the level to be calculated. The type of display is capable of managing the signal coming from the sensor and displaying the oil level state as illustrated below. Each time the battery is connected the instrument carries out a check to ascertain whether or not the sensor is present; if the sensor is not present then the instrument does not display any information relating to the oil level, whilst if the sensor is detected the instrument indicates the oil level. Speedometer The speedometer reading makes it possible to show speeds of between 0 Km/h and 180 Km/h and imperial units are also shown on the scale. The instrument panel receives the speedometer signal from an impulse generator created by means of a Hall effect sensor fitted on the gearbox flywheel. The speedometer function is achieved by means of a stepping motor operated by an electronic circuit with a clockwise direction of rotation. Rev counter The engine rev counter reading makes it possible to display values of between 0 and 6000 rpm The engine rpm signal comes from an injection/ignition electronic control unit. The instrument panel acquires this signal operating the rev counter by means of a stepping motor managed by an electronic circuit with a clockwise direction of rotation. Indicator recovery logics (stepping motors) The recovery of any steps lost by the instrument panel is guaranteed for each individual indicator. The "return to zero" logic for the pointers is verified each time the battery is disconnected/reconnected. The same recovery function is also used each time the ignition is turned on and off. Clock function The clock is the digital type with an LCD with figures with 7 segments. The time is shown in hours and minutes starting from 0:00 up to 23:59 when it then returns to 0:00. After each time the battery is connected or after the microprocessor is reset, the clock shows 0:00. If the clock adjustment button (32) is pressed for more than 2 secs, access is gained to the "clock adjustment" mode when it is released. The hours and minutes are adjusted in this mode, pressing the button for more than 1 sec increases the minutes with the time between one increment and the next varying in a linear fashion. If the button is pressed for more than 3 seconds, the increases are in 10 minute steps (approximately to the next tenth) for both the minutes and the hours. If no corrections are made for 5 seconds, the "clock adjustment" mode is exited. Engine coolant temperature gauge The engine coolant temperature reading is taken by means of a stepping motor operated by an electronic circuit with a clockwise direction of rotation with a scale that starts at "C" which corresponds to 50 degrees centrigrade and ends at "H" which is around 130 degrees centrigrade. The movement of the pointer in the red sector corresponds to a dangerous temperature of 120°C. With the ignition on the pointer shows the temperature reading according to the following logic: if T < 50 °C the pointer should be on the first scale reference. if T > 50 °C, the pointer should be positioned on the reference corresponding the temperature value measured. If the (burst of heat) condition occurs at the key-on, then the temperature reading corresponding to the position of the pointer at the key-on should be shown; later on, the pointer will reach the position corresponding to the actual temperature in an effective time of 2 mins. WARNING LIGHTS Specifications The instrument panel control unit turns the warning lights on or off by means of commands downloaded directly from sensors of components connected to the control unit. When a fault occurs, the warning lights come on in accordance with a planned strategy, but some warning lights also come on with the key ON for a period no longer than four seconds to indicate the check status of the system to which they are connected. The control panel is also equipped with some smart warning lights that are used for the air bag system fault warning light and ABS warning light Fuel level and reserve warning light The fuel gauge shows the readings as a percentage. The warning light comes on for four seconds (check stage) when the ignition is swiched on and remains on whilst the fault is received. The panel receives information directly from the fuel gauge which is located inside the tank. The two instruments are connected by a bifilar line. Fuel reserve warning light The fuel reserve condition is signalled when the fuel level reading reaches a preset value. In order to avoid tiresome flashing, the warning light comes on with a (time hysteresis) delay of 50 seconds from the moment the reserve condition is reached and goes out with a delay of 30 seconds from when the condition no longer exists. Engine coolant temperature warning light The warning light comes on for four seconds (check stage) when the ignition is swiched on and remains on whilst the fault is received. If the warning light is on this indicates that the engine coolant temperature is too high. The engine coolant overheating signal is sent to the instrument panel directly by the engine management control unit. The temperature is controlled by means of an on/off sensor. When the ignition is turned ON (from off to on). The control panel operates the coolant temperature overheating warning light each time the ignition is switched on for about 4 seconds as an initial check irrespective of the level of the engine coolant temperature overheating signal during this stage. If the overheating input remains low for more than 5 seconds, the panel switches on the warning light and operates the temperature gauge at the end of the scale. After the ignition is switched ON When the sensor is switched off the panel lights up the warning light and operates the instrument at the end of the scale. If the sensor is on, the warning light remains off and the temperature reading is the value calculated directly for values below 120°C (if the temperature is above 120°C the pointer is at the end of the scale and the warning light comes on). The warning light should go out when the ignition is switched off. Overheating signal connection diagnosis It is not possible to carry out a fault dianosis for the connection between the switch and the panel. If there is a faulty connection between the engine management control unit or the switch and the panel to prevent the warning light from coming, the instrument positions itself in the end of scale position and lights up the coolant overheating warning light when the panel calculates that the value is equal to or more than 120 degrees centigrade even though the input signal is constantly high. (no connection) The management of the warning light is different because the engine coolant overheating signal can arrive from either the engine management control unit or switch "C" which corresponds to 50 degrees centigrade and "H" which is the end of scale at about 130 degrees centigrade. Automatic transmission failure The warning light comes on for four seconds (check stage) when the ignition is swiched on and remains on whilst the fault is received. The automatic transmission failure signal is produced by the automatic transmission control unit which converses with the panel by means of a serial line at 500 bit/sec. The gear engaged is displayed by means of liquid crystal display segements which readings alternating between the symbols "P", "R", "N", "D", "1", "2", "3" and "4". The LCD for the automatic transmission continues to show the gear engaged, even when the ignition is switched off, as long as the auto. trans. control unit continues to transmit information via the serial line. Minimum engine oil pressure warning light The minimum engine oil pressure fault signal comes from a normally open type on/off sensor that operates according to the following logic: With the contact open the pressure is above the minimum level (warning light off) With the contact closed the pressure is below the minimum value (warning light on) Heater plugs warning light The heater plugs warning light (diesel engines only) comes on for four seconds when the ignition is switched on and its operation is determined by the receipt of a message from the CCM with the light on constantly when the ignition is switched on and flashing when the heater plugs failure signal is received. The warning light remains off when the message is received from the CCM even during the check stage. Injection/EOBD failure warning light The type of signal coming from the engine management control unit remains activated in failure conditions switching on the amber/red LED (depending on the version) in the panel. The EOBD warning lights remains off whilst the engine is being started as long as the fault conditions do not exist; in this case the warning light remains activated. CODE warning light The impulse that signals the failure of the alarm signal comes from the CODE control unit in which case the LED lights up amber; the timing of this warning light is managed by the actual CODE control unit according to the operating stages. Passenger Air Bag warning lights With the key ON, the yellow passenger side air bag disabled warning light comes on for about four seconds (initial self-diagnosis stage). If the control unit detects a fault in the warning light, it saves the fault code, turns on the fault warning light and maintains the passenger side airbag module disabled. System operation is restored by means of an EXAMINER as with the fault warning light. Once the initial self-diagnostic stage of 4 seconds has elapsed, if the key-operated disablement switch is turned OFF, the warning light stays on to indicate (passenger module disabled). If no faults are present, the warning light flashes for another four seconds and then goes off to indicate (passenger module enabled). The passgner Air Bag deactivated signal is produced by the Air Bag control unit. The passenger side module MUST be disabled only with the ignition key (ignition key OFF) - (DO NOT USE a second ignition key to disable). ASR/TC warning light The operating/failure signal is produced by the ABS control unit. The LED on constantly indicates either the failure of the ASR/TC system or that the system has been disabled by the user via the special button. If the light is on intermittently, this indicates that the ASR/TC is switched on. Brake pad wear warning light This red coloured warning light in the panel signals brake pad wear; it is switched on by means of a conductor countersunk into the pad friction material. When the conductor reaches the surface of the pad as a result of wear, it is short circuited to each by the brake disc during braking. ABS failure warning light The red warning light signals an ABS failure and comes on either when the fault message is received from the ABS control unit or if there is a fault in the circuit that connects the warning light to the ABS control unit. Recharging warning light This red warning light remains on for about 4 seconds when the ignition is switched on during the check stage and indicates that the alternator is not working properly. Cruise control on warning light The signal is produced by the robotized gearbox control unit and the warning light remains on when this signal is switched on. EBD/brake fluid level/handbrake applied warning light The handbrake warning light comes on constantly when the message is received from the handbrake applied sensor. The brake fluid warning light comes on constantly (with the handbrake switched off) when the insufficient brake fluid level message is received. The EBD failure warning light comes on constantly with the handbrake switched off when the EBD failure message is received. Doors open warning light The warning light comes on when the signal is received coming from a sensor activated to earth that one or more doors are open. The warning light remains on until the doors are closed. Radiator coolant low level warning light The low radiator coolant level signal comes from a normally open open/closed type sensor and is managed according to the following logic: Contact open: radiator coolant above the minimum level. Contact closed: minimum radiator coolant level. Seat belt not fastened warning light If the red seat belts warning light is on, this indicates that the seat belt is not fastened and it operates according to the following logic: with the ignition ON, if the driver has not fastened their seat belt, the warning light comes on constantly. with the ignition ON, if the seat belt is fastened before the ignition is switched on the warning light remains off. if the seat belt is unfastened whilst driving, the LED comes on constantly. The warning light is switched on directly by an N.C. switch located in the driver's belt. Main beam headlamp warning light The warning light signalling that the main beam headlamps are on is operated by receiving a message from the steering column switch unit control unit that the main beam headlamps are on/off. Side lights warning light The warning light signalling that the side lights are on is operated by receiving a message from the steering column switch unit control unit that the side lights are on/off. Direction indicator warning light The operation of the direction indicators warning light is determined by receiving a message that the direction indicators or the hazard warning lights are activated (in the latter case the warning light comes on even if the ignition is switched off) with the flashing frequency dictated by the steering column switch unit control unit. The warning light signals the function by lighting up the signals for the same family. Water in fuel filter warning light The warning light uses an LED and remains on constantly after the check stage if it receives the signal from the water in the diesel filter sensor. AIR BAG system failure warning light - At the key ON, the (red) fault warning light comes on for about four seconds (initial self-diagnosis stage) and then goes off. If the control unit detects a fault in the warning light, it saves the corresponding fault code. If no system faults are detected at key on and no fault conditions are present in the fault memory, the warning light goes off after four seconds of self-diagnosis. Otherwise it stays on until key off. The warning light stays or comes on durng normal car operation in the following cases: the control unit detects a fault in the airbag system; the control unit detects a crash with system activation; when a fault is detected in the warning light connection circuit.

COMPOSITION The vehicle is equipped with a frontal and side (optional) protection system which is activated following impacts of medium intensity to ensure the safety of the occupants of the front seats. To complete the safety system and to improve the restraint system the vehicle is also fitted with front seat belt pretensioners with load restricters. The control unit control system allwos the total or partial activation of the devices in the case of a frontal impact. The (Breed) protection system comprises: 3 pretensioners, driver's, front side passenger and front centre passenger, respectively; A driver's Air Bag; A passenger Air Bag (with the task of protecting the front passenger and the centre front passenger); 2 side impact sensors (one on each side) A passenger Air Bag disabling switch 2 side Air Bags (side bags, one on each side) Two pretensioners (driver and passenger) and a driver's Air Bag are fitted as standard on the vehicle. The control unit manages the accumulation of energy for the front Air Bags and memorizes both the fault codes and the crash codes. The red coloured fault warning light in the instrument panel is the intelligent type. The control unit does not have to be replaced if the pretensioners or the Side Bags are activated up to three times. If the front Air Bags only are activated and when the pretensioners and/or side bags are activated for the third time, the control unit has to be replaced. It is designed to recognise an impact situation in plenty of time to activate the pretensioners alone or the pretensioners plus the air bag modules according to impact severity and type. The control unit is rigidly secured to the body beneath the central car consule near the centre of gravity. This location allows interior deceleration sensors to detect car deceleration with accuracy. The control unit should always be fitted with the arrow, stamped on the adhesive plate, facing the direction of travel of the vehicle. Always check that there are no foreign bodies between the control unit and the bodyshell and tighten the fixing bolts to the recommended torque. Composition The control unit contains two deceleration sensors, one electronic and one electromechanical safety sensor that activates an activation enablement function independently of the electronic sensor. If the car deceleration level detected by the electronic sensor and processed by the ECU in terms of impact severity, exceeds the severity level set for the device deactivation control, the control unit allows the command to be sent only if the safety sensor is closed at the same moment. The following functions are present to ensure the system is correctly managed: energy accumulation: the control unit is supplied at 12V with the key ON but can still operate for a few fractions of a second if the power supply is cut off or experiences a voltage drop in order to safeguard system operation and write the data in the crash memory. check earth fastening: the control unit software checks the electrical contact between body and control unit; fault memory: with the key ON, the control unit continuously monitors circuit operation (including energy reserve circuits) during normal vehicle operation and impacts. It also diagnoses all electrical parts of the system and indicates the presence of faults by turning on an airbag system fault warning light on the instrument panel and saving the fault code. crash memory: records information on crash events that trigger activation of the pretensioners and front or side modules. DRIVER'S AIR BAG MODULE The following figure shows an assembly view 1 - Casing 2 - Connector The driver side air bag is a passive safety device. It takes the form of a bag that inflates automatically in the case of frontal impact to interpose itself between the driver's body and front passenger compartment structures. The Air Bag module is fitted in the centre of the steering wheel. The module comprises: a plastic cover that tears at preset points when activated to allow the bag to expand correctly. a bag which has a volume of around 60 litres a pyrotechnic type gas generator a containment case. Operation The module gas inflation generator is electrically activated by means of a signal from the electronic control module. Following this signal a pyrotechnic charge housed in the generator is primed. The gases produced by the combustion of the charge flow through special openings and expand in the bag causing the cover to break at specified points. When fully inflated, the bag is in an optimal position to protect the occupant. After the bag is inflated by the gases it immediately deflates thanks to the presence of suitably located breather openings. PASSENGER AIR BAG The following figure shows an assembly view 1 - Left connection point 2 - Right connection point Operation The passenger Air Bag is located in the dashboard and is designed to protect the two front pasengers. It consists of a module comprising two gas generators that have the task of inflating a very large single bag (about 120 litres) whose shape is designed to protect the occupants of both the centre and side seats. This solution allows the optimum protection of both occupants. The composition and operation are the same as for the driver's Air Bag, with with two gas generators in place of the single one for the driver's air bag fitted in the steering wheel. A plastic flap that is incorporated in the dashboard allows the bag to escape as it inflates in the direction of the driver. SATELLITE SENSOR SIDE BAG SYSTEM The Side Bags are illustrated in the diagram below 1. Side Bag casing 2. Driver's seat Operation The Side Bag modules are fitted in the door side front seat backrests. To ensure maximum front seat occupant safety in the case of side impact, side bag modules are installed on the seat squabs. They are fitted on the side facing the outside of the car beneath the trim. This configuration is considered one of the most effective because it ensures the airbag is always in optimum position in relation to the occupant regardless of seat setting or occupant size. The side bag mainly protects the chest and abdomen, even if the seat occupant is not sitting properly because bag opening dynamics minimise the risk of body damage caused by impact with the airbag. The side bag module consists of a plastic container that houses the gas generator and a permeable nylon bag. The module container includes a cover with preset break points. When the seat cover is fitted, the exterior of the trim in the area over the bags includes seams designed to yield easily. The connection between the module and the electrical system takes place by means of two cables with a yellow outer casing housed together with the connecting cable. The module inflation gas generator is electrically activated by a signal coming from the electronic control unit. The signal is managed by satellite sensors, located in the centre pillars, which detect direct impact acceleration along the transverse axis of the vehicle and send it to the control unit. Following this signal, a pyrotechnic activation is set off that causes the gas in the generator to expand and inflate the bag. The increase in bag volume breaks the container in the set areas and causes the squab cover seams to yield along the preset sections to allow the bag to emerge correctly. When fully inflated, the bag is in an optimal position to protect the occupant. The bag deflates immediately after being inflated by the gas because the fabric is permeable. It is not possible to carry out operations on seats fitted with air bags, apart from seat removal/refitting. It is strictly forbidden to dismantle seats fitted with air bags. This operation must be carried by trained, authorised technical personnel. Do not cover the front seat squab with extra covers. Do not wash the seat squab with water or steam under pressure. CLOCK SPRING The clock spring is a device that allows the leads connecting the air bag module and the other electrical controls installed on the steering wheel to follow steering wheel rotation without danger of breaking. The clock spring has two cables on the steering wheel side with one designed to connect the Air Bag module and one for connecting the steering wheel electrical functions. Operation Inside the two plates, the leads connecting the air bag module are wound into a spiral with sufficient coils to follow the steering wheel rotations. The upper plate is turned by fasteners on the inside of the retaining ring that fit into the seat on the steering wheel hub. In working position, the steering wheel presses on the ring to release it from its fasteners and thus allow both plates to turn freely. When the steering wheel is removed, the spring-loaded ring locks rotation between both plates. This function prevents the upper plate, now no longer secured to the steering wheel, from turning freely and unwinding or winding the coil inside the device and possibly causing it to break. The following must be observed during operations that require removal of the steering wheel and device. always work with the car's wheels aligned straight ahead. lock the cable, for safety reasons, using a band before removing it from the steering column switch unit. If the upper plate should turn in relation to the lower plate for any reason so that the exact starting position is no longer certain, the clock spring MUST be replaced. SEAT BELT PRETENSIONERS The pretensioners are pyrotechnic devices that are activated electrically by means of a signal from the electronic control unit. They are built into the reel of the front and rear side seat belts. When the pretensioners cut in following frontal impact above a certain threshold, the seat belt straps are retracted to hold the occupant as closely as possible against the seat squab. Operation When the car decelerates to a sufficient extent, the electronic sensor in the electronic control unit sends a signal to trigger the gas generator pyrotechnic charges (5). Combustion of propellent (6) develops a chemical reaction that produces inert gas. Gas pressure then generates a force that pushes the piston rack upward (4). The rack turns a toothed wheel (1) connected to toothed wheel (2). This meshes with toothed bush (3) to change the rotary motion of the chuck so that it turns in the opposite direction to the direction which the belt unwinds and rewinds the belt by a few centimetres. Once the pretensioners have been activated, the belts are locked and must be replaced. AIR BAG SYSTEM FAILURE WARNING LIGHT AND PASSENGER AIR BAG DISABLED WARNING LIGHT The two warning lights in the instrument panel are illustrated in the diagram below 1 - Passenger Air Bag disabled warning light 2 - Air Bag failure warning light Fault warning light The operation of the Air Bag system failure warning light is known as intelligent because it is also capable of signalling a faulty connection with the control unit. At key ON, the fault warning light (red) comes on for about four seconds (initial self-diagnosis stage) and then goes off. If the control unit detects a fault in the warning light, it memorizes the corresponding fault code. After the four seconds of the self-diagnosis stage, if the system does not detect any errors, the warning light goes out; if errors are detected, it remains on until the ignition is next switched off. The warning light stays or comes on durng normal car operation in the following cases: the control unit detects a fault in the airbag system; the control unit detects a crash with system activation; when a fault is detected in the warning light connection circuit. As a consequence of a crash when the pretensioners or sidebags alone are activated, the warning light stays on until system operating conditions are restoered (replacement of affected part or control unit repair using an EXAMINER) If the crash causes the front airbag modules to activate, the warning light stays on permanently because the control unit cannot reset (in this case the control unit must be replaced). If internal operating errors occur during the operational lifetime of the control unit that cannot be repaired during the EXAMINER, this are indicated by permanent activation of the warning light. Passenger front AIR BAG disabled warning light With the key ON, the yellow passenger side air bag disabled warning light comes on for about four seconds (initial self-diagnosis stage). If the control unit detects a fault in the warning light, it saves the fault code, turns on the fault warning light and maintains the passenger side airbag module disabled. System operation is restored by means of an EXAMINER as with the fault warning light. Once the initial self-diagnostic stage of 4 seconds has elapsed, if the key-operated disablement switch is turned OFF, the warning light stays on to indicate that the passenger module is disabled. If no faults are present, the warning light flashes for another four seconds and then goes off to indicate that the passenger module is enabled. The passenger side module MUST be disabled only with the ignition key (ignition key OFF) - (DO NOT USE a second ignition key to disable).

SPECIFICATIONS The parking TV camera is located in the rear of the vehicle on the rear roof beam. This device ensures a rear view only during reverse activation. The main aim of the TV rear view system is to aid the driver during parking manoeuvres. The system allows users who have engaged reverse to carry out manoeuvres while observing the view on the Connect display. The resulting view is a mirror-image (as provided by the rear view mirror). The system consists of: TV camera with optical unit, protection against atmospheric and environmental agents, connection leads, multifunction display (built into Connect). microswitch on gearbox. 1 - TV camera 2 - Reversing sensor 3 - Connect COMPOSITION The TV camera consists of: outer protective shell (1), gaskets (2), protective glass (3) electronic circuit (4), electrical wiring (5). OPERATION A TV image is displayed with key ON (but not during start-up) and reverse engaged. TV operation is automatically disabled when reverse is disengaged. The function is disabled: with key Off, if battery voltage drops below a minimum threshold, during engine start-up, when reverse is disengaged. The TV camera is supplied iwith power only when in use. The TV operating range is between -20°C and +80°C, but above +65°C image quality may be slightly reduced. This reduction will, however, disappear when the temperature is reduced. The TV camera is supplied with power via the Connect system (500mA, 12 ± 2V), to which it supplies, in turn, a composite video signal via a coaxial cable. If the vehicle is stove-painted, it is however advisable to remove the TV camera as a precaution. SPECIFICATIONS The new generation tachographs are of a modular construction and consist of individual components 1 - recording unit: modular tachograph; 2 - pulse generator for tachograph; 3 - tachograph discs. 4 - instrument panel; In addition to monitoring the speed and recording the route the tachograph also records four hourly groups: driving times; all other operating times; availability; pauses and rest times. The respective hourly groups are selected by driver 1 and driver 2 using the controls. The following is shown on the display: date; time; total mileage hourly groups used; symbols for the tachograph discs inserted. The diagnostic function includes controlling the system and automatically advises if there is an error with a component or service. The menu contents for the diagnostic data can be recalled using the control buttons The instrument panel usually shows the (analogue) speed and the route (total milometer). There is an option for displaying the daily mileage or a clock. The impulse generator transforms the transmission revs into impulses and transmits them to the tachograph in the form of real time signals together with the encrypted data. The impulse generator and the tachograph form a secure tamper-proof unit. Depending on the time, the tachograph disc also documents the speed, the route and the following four hourly groups: driving time; further working time; times of availability; intervals and resting times. General system specifications General specifications: readings and recording units are separate; recording units in DIN ISO 7736 radio format; automatic recording of driving time; automatic signalling of system faults in LC display: faults in electronic components, mechanical components, instruments, interfaces and speedometer impulse generator; automatic adjustment of faults on the tachograph disc; automatic switching off of recording of hourly groups / journey after 25 hours; check on impulse generator signal with microprocessor control; multi-function display with 2 x 16 positions; two control panels for the tachograph; fixed/adjustable compartment; fixed value memory for necessary parameters such as equipment variations, adaptation, mesuring field, etc. real time battery-operated clock with automatic switching to and from summertime, specifically designed for different countries, programmed for 5 years; automatic pursuit of tachograph disc housing. 1 - Display 2 - Lead plates (test and programming interface located behind); 3 - Compartment release button; 4 - Button for adjusting desired hourly group for driver 1; 5 - Button for adjusting desired hourly group for driver 2; 6 - Button for selecting the desired menu (multifunction); 7 - Return button, one step at a time; 8 - Forward button, one step at a time; 9 - fixed/adjustable compartment. The display is lit up when the ignition is turned on. The standard display permanently shows the date, the time, the total mileage and also the symbols indicating that the tachograph discs are inserted and the hourly group is set for drivers 1 and 2. If necessary, it is possible to display the individual menu points such as the errors memory, programming data, etc. An error symbol automatically signals an event or problem. Menu functions The individual menu points can be recalled, depending on the user, in two different ways: user mode (for the driver); service mode (for service personnel). The user mode can be selected direcly by pressing button M6. The menu structure sequence is as follows: standard reading; time change (select/modify using + or - button); error memorizing (scan using + or - button). To return to the standard reading, keep button M6 pressed for more than 2 seconds. The service mode can be selected directly by pressing button M6 and switching on within 3 seconds. The menu structure sequence is as follows: standard reading; time change (select/modify using + or - button); error memorizing (scan using + or - button). UTC / status information; data programming (scan using + or - button). beginning/end of summer-time (scan using + or - button); To return to the standard reading, keep button M6 pressed for more than 2 seconds. The code UTC stands for Universal Time Coordinated Adjusting the time "Adjusting the time" menu select using button M(6) activate the adjustment of the time using the + or - button (the minutes reading will start to flash). Change the minutes: set the minutes using the + or - button, keep the button pressed until the desired value appears. determine the value set by keeping button M(6) pressed for more than 2 seconds (after which the initial display will appear). Change the hours: press button M(6) briefly (the hours reading will start to flash). set the hours using the + or - button, keep the button pressed until the desired value appears. determine the value set by keeping button M pressed for more than 2 seconds (after which the initial display will appear). Changing the time will have the following effect: the offset time displayed in menu 3 "UTC/status information" will have changed as a result of the new setting, the programmed UTC time will not be affected. The date will be automatically corrected after midnight. The automatic pursuit of the tachograph disc housing is only carried out if: it is switched on with the vehicle stationary; there is no tachograph disc in the tachograph; the compartment is closed. If the automatic pursuit of the tachograph disc has not been carried out, the time shown on the display will flash and the error symbol will be displayed. Errors memory By recalling the errors memory in service mode, the errors recorded will be shown on the display, complete with the number of errors, the date and the time when they last occurred. If the tachograph is in user mode, the display will only show the errors activated without the number of errors. 1 - Date when the error last occurred; 2 - Time when the error last occurred; 3 - Symbol to go back; 4 - Symbol to go forward; 5 - Symbol with error code; 6 - Error activated symbol; 7 - Number of errors, error presentation frequency (max. 126 recordings). "Errors memory" menu: select using button M(6) Recall individual errors: to go forward, press the + button; to go back, press the - button; press button M(6) for more than 2 seconds to return to the initial display. Impulse generator for tachograph The impulses sent by the impulse generator are used for recording the route and the speed. This type of impulse generator is activated by the gearbox output. There are different types of thread available for the fitting. Impulse generator specifications: contact-free measuring process for integrated impulse generators; transmission of impulse generator serial number and control in tachograph; data protection thanks to the DES (Data Encryption Standard) coding procedure (2 - 56); comparison of real time signal with coded signal in tachograph. Tachograph disc Description of the tachograph disc. When working alongside two drivers the recording of the hourly groups for the second driver takes place on the second driver disc. 1 - Detection of compartment opening (each opening is documented on the tachograph disc for the first driver). 2 - Speed km/h (during the journey). 3 - Recording of the time groups: driving times, further operating times, ready for use times (pause times, accompanying time, cabin rest time during the journey). Rest intervals and times. 4 - Routes calculated; each upwards and downwards recording corresponds to 5 km (If the pause time and rest time group is set and the ignition is switched off, the journey recording is interrupted). The recording of the rotation frequency takes place at the rear of the tachograph disc for driver 1 if a tachograph with an additional device for recording the rotation frequency is used. 1 - Range for the number of checks (homologation marks); 2 - Internal range; 3 - Rpm frequency recording; 4 - Ignition on/off markings Change of drivers If the driver changes vehicles during their work shift, they must take the tachograph disc with them and make a note of this change on the back of the actual disc. If the crew swaps and the second driver takes over the driving, the tachograph discs must be changed over. The first driver (who has now become the second driver) should insert their tachograph disc under the separator support and the second driver (who has now become the first driver) should insert theirs above this support. If the first or the second driver leaves the vehicle, they must take their tachograph disc with them. The new first driver (or the new second driver) should insert their tachograph disc above the separator support (under it for the second driver). If there is no second driver, position the time groups at the rest times. If the first and second drivers both leave the vehicle, each of them should remove their tachograph disc from the unit. The new vehicle crew (first and/or second driver) should place their tachograph discs in the appropriate positions. SEATS Specifications - The seats are of vital importance in terms of comfort and safety: they are, in effect, the element that has to absorb the kinetic energy acquired by the body through the effect of stresses when cornering and during acceleration/deceleration. The structure of the seats has been designed to assist and complete the protection offered by the occupant protection system. The front seats have a robust frame under the cushion which has the task of maintaining correct support for the occupant in the case of a frontal impact and of minimizing the distortion of the seat.- The cushion support frame and the special shape of the cushion base prevents the passengers from sliding under the seat belt lap strap in the case of strong deceleration known as the so-called anti-submarining effect. Composition - The exploded view of the driver's seat is illustrated in the diagram 1 - Backrest cover2 - Cushion cover3 - Backrest upholstery4 - Cushion upholstery5 - Armrest6 - Lumbar adjustment mechanism7 - Backrest frame8 - Lumbar adjustment knob9 - Backrest adjustment knob10 - Cushion frame11 - Seat lifting mechanism12 - Rear cushion height adjustment lever13 - Rear cushion height adjustment knob14 - Front cushion height adjustment lever15 - Front cushion height adjustment knob16 - Seat lengthwise adjustment guides17 - Rear additional heater18 - Seat support structure Front seats - In the front part of the seating area there is an excellent structure for anti-submarining, to prevent the body sliding forward under the seat belt in the case of severe frontal impacts.- This also contributes to limiting injury to the abdomen and femur by reducing the body's forward acceleration.- To assist back support the driver's seat only has a modern support system (6) for the lumbar region specially designed and extended to wrap around the back and support it. A special knob (8) on the backrest is used for adjustments.- The driver's seat cushion can be height adjusted using two control levers; using knob (15) it is possible to adjust the height of the front part of the seat whilst knob (13) allows the height adjustment of the rear section.- The angle of the backrest is adjusted using a rotary knob (9). Heated front seats - The heated seat (where fitted) is equipped with a heater pad located between the seat upholstery and the cover; this heater pad heats the cushion and the backrest at the same time. - The heating of the seat is activated by means of a special control located on the actual seat casing. 1 - Backrest cover2 - Cushion cover3 - Backrest upholstery4 - Cushion upholstery5 - Heater pad

With the ignition, the ABS warning light and the handbrake warning light come on simultaneously and stay on for longer than 3 seconds (both warning lights should go off after the initial control unit test) The low brake fluid level and handbrake warning light also indicates an EBD fault if it comes on at the same time as the ABS warning light Under these circumstances, the rear wheels may lock and the vehicle may skid if the brakes are operated because the system EBD function is temporarily deactivated. If it comes on by itself, this means that the handbrake is on or the brake fluid level is too low 1 CHECK USING DIAGNOSTIC EQUIPMENT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Connect the diagnostic test equipment (Examiner or other instruments) to the tester input. Check that there are no faults in the ABS control unit. Move on to Step 2 1. Error detected in the control unit 1. Continue following the instructions for the diagnostic equipment 2. No communication with the control unit 2. Restore the connection between the ABS control unit and the diagnostic connector 2 CHECK ON CORRECT OPERATION ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the fault is no longer present End of diagnosis

When starting, the Air Bag failure warning light comes on and stays on for longer than 4 seconds (the warning light should go off after the initial control unit test) The warning light will stay on if an impact of a certain severity causes the activation of the system. The control unit must be replaced because its memory cannot be deleted The Air Bag warning light is the smart type with a control circuit inside the panel that ensures the warning light is properly connected to the control unit.

When the engine is set to METHANE mode using the appropriate selector, the engine does not run for as long as indicated

Check that the pump supply voltage at the pump connector is 12V See E5050 DIESEL ENGINES ELECTRONIC MANAGEMENT Measure the pump absorption current by positioning the ammeter clip for the Examiner equipment on the pump supply cable (at the fuse box or directly on the pump inlet cable) The current measured should be between 2 and 10 Ampere.
Disconnect the electrical connection for the solenoid valve on the methane canister and check that the coil winding resistance is 11.50 Ohm ± 20 % at 20°C.

Selezionare il funzionamento a metano. Mantenendo il motore acceso, sollevare la vettura con il ponte. Chiudere tutti i rubinetti delle bombole eccetto uno (procedere in ordine partendo con quello di sinistra). Attendere per circa 1 minuto. Se la vettura non commuta a benzina riprendere dal punto 3) lasciando aperto un altro rubinetto e mantenendo sempre chiusi gli altri. Se la vettura commuta a benzina significa che l'elettrovalvola della bombola con il rubinetto aperto è bloccata chiusa. Procedere quindi con l'attivazione della stessa con la diagnosi attiva, il controllo del cablaggio/connessioni ed eventualmente controllare la resistenza della bobina.

The operation test involves carrying out an overall power uptake test for the following loads:+ LPG pump; Solenoid on LPG cylinder Proceed as follows: With all loads deactivated, measure battery voltage and ensure that no-load voltage is at least 12.8 V . Otherwise charge the battery. Turn the ignition key to the OFF position; Fit an ammeter probe to the battery negative lead. Disconnect the LPG pump current sensor from the connector Connect the connector terminal connected to the current sensor V to the battery +12 V via a bridge with a 15 A fuse interposed. Check that overall load uptake is: approximately 4 A with the LPG tank empty; approximately 6.5 A with the tank full of LPG. Switching to LPG is inhibited if current uptake by the LPG pump does not exceed a threshold of 4 A , corresponding to tank condition when not empty.

Disconnect the electrical connection between the LPG tank and control panel and check for the following between pins 1 and 2 of the tank side connection : ohmmic resistance value less than 3000 Ohm ; and an ohmmic resistance value greater than 900 Ohm .
Secure the valve in a vice. Close the jaws with the float in lowered position. Blow air from the charge fitting. Lift up the float with your left hand and check the air flow is interrupted.

Check LPG pressure sensor K053 With the ignition switched on, check that the sensor supply is about 5 Volt . With the engine running, check that the sensor output voltage signal is between 1 and 4V . DESCRIPTION CONNECTOR - LPG pressure sensor

Make sure that the ignition key is in the OFF position, then disconnect the negative battery terminal (-). Disconnect the solenoid electrical connection and check the coil winding resistance is between 19 and 21 Ohm at 20 °C .

Check LPG cut out solenoid valve L063 Make sure that the ignition key is in the OFF position, then disconnect the negative battery terminal (-). Disconnect the electrical connection for the solenoid valve and check that the solenoid valve coil winding resistance is 19 and 21 Ohm at 20°C .
Disconnect the electrical connection for the solenoid valve on the reduction unit and check that the coil winding resistance is 8 Ohm ± 20 % at 20°C.

Position the three-way connector 1870685000 between the low pressure pipe and the methane distribution manifold (after having moved the power assisted steering fluid reservoir sideways). Connect a pressure gauge with a 1/2" attachment and a 16 bar end of scale. Let the engine run smoothly and check that the pressure is 8 and 10 bar . If the pressure is lower, also check that the pressure upstream of the reduction unit is not more than 15 bar . If this is the case, then the reduction unit is faulty.

Remember to follow all the safety regulations set out and, above all, to keep lamps or devices that could produce sparks or electrical discharges at a safe distance. In order to carry out the test correctly, the LPG pressure downstream of the injectors must be less than or equal to 5 bar . For this purpose, proceed as described below: Disconnect the connector for the solenoid valve from the LPG return line. Disconnect the connector for the solenoid valve from the supply line. Position the Gas/petrol selector to Gas mode. Start the engine and wait for the system to switch to LPG and then back again to petrol. Connect to the diagnostic equipment in the "Control Units Test" mode. Enter the "Parameters" ambient. Check that the "Gas Pressure" parameter is less than or equal to 5 bar . If the pressure is still high, repeat the cycle. Turn the ignition key to the OFF position. Disconnect the battery negative and positive terminals and connect them to ground using a cable. Disconnect the connectors from the LPG injectors Remove the pipe retaining bands. Remove the LPG distribution manifold keeping the supply and return pipes connected. Remove the band for the connector pipe with the manifold and remove the latter. Introduce a small amount of oil into the test injector spray jet. Check that there are no gas leaks which would show up in the form of a series of oil bubbles.

The electrical check is carried out by placing a bridge (2) to be constructed in situ (not supplied as spares) between the sensor (1) and the connector (3) in order to supply the sensor and receive the output signal using a multimeter (voltmeter). Place the bridge between the sensor and the connector. With the ignition switched on, check that the sensor supply is about 5 Volt . Check that the output voltage is between 0.5 V (with the tank full) and 4.5 V with the canisters completely full at a pressure of 200 bar .
Make sure that the ignition key is in the OFF position. Disconnect the electrical connection for the injector. Check the coil resistance is between 4.1 and 5.1 Ohm at 20 °C .

Connect the tester. Select "methane gas injection" in the "Control Unit Test" mode. Identify the item "Methane pressure" in the parameter list. With the engine running, measure the pressure and check that it is at least 15 bar , with the canisters nearly empty and a maximum of 220 bar , with the canisters completely full. It should be remembered that the pressure in the canisters is also affected by the ambient temperature, if the temperature is low then the pressure is low.

Set up the diagnostic equipment to produce a voltage graph (select the voltmeter function on the "Instruments" menu) Disconnect the rpm sensor connector. Connect the connector to the sensor using "Disconnecting switch " AD 223 n° 18.063.88000 . Using the diagnostic equipment probes, connect between pin 1 and 2 of the disconnecting switch. Press the Start button on the diagnostic equipment to begin creating a graph Check that signal amplitude is greater than 1.5 V and that the graph is as specified during engine start-up.

Connect the tester pressure transducer between the diesel filter and the pressure pump (connect it to the filter outlet). Turn the ignition key ON . Within 30 seconds , check that the pressure on the pressure gauge is between 2 and 3 bars . The tank pump will go off after 30 seconds. Make sure that the taps and the adjustment screws at the side of the pressure gauge are open (except the ones on ducts not connected to the system). Connect the tester pressure transducer between the diesel filter and the pressure pump (connect it to the filter outlet). Turn the ignition key ON . Within 30 seconds , check that the pressure on the pressure gauge is between 0.6 and 0.7 bars . The tank pump will go off after 30 seconds. Make sure that the taps and the adjustment screws at the side of the pressure gauge are open (except the ones on ducts not connected to the system).

Disconnect the electrical connections from all the injectors. Disconnect the fuel recirculation pipes from all the injectors. Constrict the injector recirculation pipe so that no fuel comes out during the test. Connect the tester. Display the " measured diesel pressure " and “ engine rpm ” in the parameter screen of the “ Control unit test ” section. Turn the ignition key to START for 5 seconds and check that the fuel pressure is greater than 300 bar with engine rpm equal to 200 rpm .

Fit the tool 1.870.737.000 between the air hose and the air chamber. Connect the pressure transducer to the tool. Position the diagnostic equipment in the passenger compartment and make the connections. Select "pressure gauge" on the diagnostic equipment and prepare for the acquisition of data in "intake pressure" mode with a 2000 mmHg end of scale and selection time of 10 seconds . Road test the vehicle (sticking to the speed limits in force) as follows: with a motorway journey: let the vehicle reach 2500 rpm in 4th gear; initiate the acquistion by pressing start on the diagnostic equipment and about 2 seconds later fully depress the accelerator pedal until the engine speed is 3500 rpm ; once this speed is reached completely release the accelerator pedal; display the resulting graph and in the pressure constant section, with the exception of the initial peak, the reading should be 1900 -2080 mbar (1444 -1581 mmHg) corresponding to a supercharging value of 900 -1080 mbar . during an out of town journey at a fast speed: let the vehicle reach 2500 rpm in 3rd gear; initiate the acquistion by pressing start on the diagnostic equipment and about 2 seconds later fully depress the accelerator pedal until the engine speed is 3500 rpm ; once this speed is reached completely release the accelerator pedal; display the resulting graph and in the pressure constant section, with the exception of the initial peak, the reading should be 1900 -2080 mbar (1444 -1581 mmHg) corresponding to a supercharging value of 900 -1080 mbar . The vehicle owner is obliged to check the tachograph at intervals and have its operation checked at least once every two years, e.g. when the vehicle undergoes a technical service. Any operation that involves modification and/or replacement of system parts must therefore be carried out by personnel who are authorised to test the system. After each check, ensure the plate is changed and contains the required information. Messages The tachograph continually monitors system operation and automatically indicates any faults that may occur in the controls or in one of the components. The tachograph display shows an exclamation mark beside the mileometer and, according to the type of error, displays a time indication or the colon between the figures stops flashing. The messages and indications may be displayed immediately after closing the cassette or whenever they appear on the display. To display the error message code: The function may be called up only with the car at a standstill! Select the "Error Memory" menu by giving the key marked "M" two short presses. The other active errors may be displayed using the + or - keys. When the screen displays: la data (giorno. mese. ultime due cifre dell'anno), l'ora di inizio dell'errore, una icona con il simbolo più (+) ad indicare se sono presenti altri errori, il codice errore. To exit the "Error Memory" simply press the "M" button for longer than two seconds or do not press any key for 20 seconds. Faults in the recording and writing system Some error codes with associated fault descriptions are given below. 9061: Defective operation (1) of vehicle speed graphic recorder. 9062: Error in the multiple graphic recorder (MFS) Defective operation (2) 9063: Faullt in graphic recorder lift system (SAS) (3) Update of disc carrier adjustment. Open the cassette and remove both discs, then re-close the cassette. The tachograph automatically updates the disc holder times, the error code and times stop flashing. Open the cassette again and insert new discs if necessary. The tachograph is ready to operate again. The message disappers automatically only after the cause has been eliminated, e.g. in the case of an error by the driver/user. If the error is continuously repeated, replace the tachograph ensuring standards and certifications are observed. Adjusting the tachograph power cut-out Some error codes with associated fault descriptions are given below. A400: If power has been restored, the device displays a thick line (4) on the tachograph disc shortly after start-up (first sensor pulse). no service error is present, the driver 1 tachograph disc is therefore present and the cassette is closed. Power cut When power is restored, the device traces out a line (4) on the tachograph disc. If the error is continuously repeated, replace the tachograph ensuring standards and certifications are observed. Break in communication between the tachograph and speedometer pulse generator, Some error codes with associated fault descriptions are given below. A423: No input/output data signal - As soon as the vehicle is stationary, the marking (5) appears. The recording to the vehicle speed graph is resumed when the vehicle is in motion. A822: No signal in real time: - The marking (6) appears immediately after the fault appears and remains until the cause is eliminated. The time set is continuously adjusted (from data signals). The last time setting is recorded. A423: No I/O data signal and no real time signal. The marking (8) appears immediately after the fault has occurred. A radial line (7) appears in the panel to adjusting the route. The last time set is recorded. These error markings are recorded until the cause of the error has been removed. Marking (6) appears immediately after the fault arises and continues until the cause is eliminated or after vehicle motion has stopped.

With the Examiner in Instrument mode and set to the Voltmeter function, check that the TV camera power supply (battery voltage +12 Volt) is present at the Overtaking Sensor control unit output. For the next test, the Examiner power supply negative terminal must be connected to the vehicle earth. Connect the positive contact (red) of the Examiner to the central coaxial lead wire leading from the TV camera and the negative contact (black) to the vehicle earth. Turn on the Examiner, select Instrument mode and the Voltmeter function, then select full scale deflection of 20 volt and a time base of 1 second (measurement to be carried out with the TV camera activated and the lens covered by a dark cloth). Then capture the coaxial cable signal graph. Enlarge the resulting voltage graph until the shape resembles the drawing shown below. Check that the voltage and time values are similar to those shown in the drawing. If the waveform is not as described, this may be due to several possible faults: If the recorded graph trace is very close to zero (fluctuating from - 0.15 Volts to + 0.15 Volts) as shown in the following drawing. The line (i.e. the coaxial cable from the TV camera) is short-circuited between the central conductor and the external earth or the TV camera is faulty. If the recorded voltage graph trace is far from zero (voltage fluctuates between -20 Volts and +20 Volts). The line (i.e. the coaxial cable from the TV camera) is in open circuit or the central conductor and/or earth are not connected or the TV camera is faulty. Carry out the same test at the TV camera terminals (without opening the external case) to rule out possible wiring faults.

With the Examiner in Instrument mode and set to the Voltmeter function, check that the parking TV camera power supply (battery voltage +12 volts) is present at the Connect output. For the next test, connect the Examiner negative power supply terminal to the vehicle earth. Connect the postive contact (red) of the Examine to the central wire of the coaxial cable leading from the parking TV camera, and the negative contact (black) to the vehicle earth. Turn on the Examiner and select the Voltmeter function while in Instrument mode. Select full scale deflection of 20 volts and a time base of 1 s (measure with TV camera on and lens covered by a dark cloth). Then plot a graph of the signal on the coaxial cable. Enlarge the resulting voltage graph until the shape is similar to the following drawing Check that the voltage and time values are similar to the drawing. Although images are not displayed on the Connect screen, the Examiner tester states that the parking TV camera is working and the cause must therefore lie in the Connect system If the wave form is not as described, this may indicate several possible faults: if the graph plot is very close to zero (fluctuates between - 0.15 Volt and + 0.15 Volt) as shown in the following drawing, the line (coaxial cable leading from the parking TV camera) must be short-circuited between the central wire and the external mass or the TV camera is faulty If the voltage graph plot is far from zero (fluctuations with voltages greater than - 20 Volts and +20 Volts). The line (coaxial cable leading from the parking TV camera) is in open circuit, i.e. the central wire and/or earth are not connected, or the TV camera is faulty. Carry out the same tests at the TV camera terminals to rule out possible wiring faults.
