Description A Webasto "Thermo Top C that operates completely independently of the engine is available as an accessory. This device makes it possible to: heat the coolant and therefore the engine; heat the passenger compartment and thus defrost the windows. Device installation requires the heater unit to be connected to the engine cooling, fuel feed and vehicle electrical system interface systems. The system consists of: a heating unit that essentially consists of a diesel burner; an silencer for fuel combustion exhaust gases; a metering pump fitted on the fuel return pipe that delivers fuel to the burner; a heat exchanger, coaxial to the burner, connected via the vehicle coolant system; an output pipe from the metering pump to the metering device; an electronic control unit for controlling and regulating auxiliary heater system functions built into the heater unit; a digital timer for programming the heater activation time or for immediate manual activation. The power supply to the heater is protected by special fuses located in the optional junction unit under the instrument facia.

Operational Description Webasto control unit M075 receives a power supply directly from the battery supplied by programming device H110, supplied in turn by a line protected by fuse F58 located in optional junction unit B101. The heater pump is ignition-operated and fully managed by control unit M075 or device H110. The ignition-operated supply is governed by relay T24, also housed in optional junction unit B101. The relay is "normally closed" type; i.e. relay pins 30 and 87 are short-circuited at rest. When inertia switch I050 cuts in, the earth reference at pin 86 is no longer present. Under these conditions, the coil is no longer excited and the internal relay contact opens. Under these conditions, the pump of heater N044 is no longer supplied from the battery. This strategy is used as a precaution to prevent or at least reduce the risk of fire in the case of accidents. Sensor K042 supplies control unit M075 with external air temperature readings that are used to ensure correct heater system operation. Control unit M075 supplies the supplementary heater motors, where present in the vehicle, from pin F to provide a direct power supply from the battery via shunt J035.

Description The vehicle climate control system is achieved through the duct/distributor unit and heater.The air conditioning system integrates the heater with the function of producing cold and dehumidified air achieved by switching on the compressor and the cooling system.The climate is controlled by means of three control knobs on the facia:The left-hand knob controls air ventilation at four different speeds by means of an electrical control;the centre knob controls the mechanical warm and cold air mixing flap;the right hand knob controls opening of the flaps that govern air flow distribution mechanically via a cable.The control for different fan speeds is via a resistance partitioner protected against temperature surges by a thermal fuse.A cursor under the knobs on the control unit modulates the recirculation function mechanically via a cable.The control unit is lit with the side lights on.The entire system is protected by dedicated fuses housed in the engine bay and under-facia junction units. Fan activation is governed by a specific relay.The fan can only be activated with the key ON.

Operational Description The climate control system control unit M070 receives an ignition-operated supply at pin 3 along the line protected by fuse F31 located in the engine compartment junction unit B001. When the climate control fan selector H081 is turned to select the first, second or third speed the passenger compartment air fan adjustment resistance O030 receives a reference earth.The remote control switch H022 protects the passenger compartment air fan N085: when the maximum speed is switched on and the high speed remote control switch J041 contact is closed, the passenger compartment air fan remote control switch J022 switches the position of its contact and the passenger compartment air fan N085, initially supplied and protected by the line for fuse F55 located in the junction unit under the dashboard B002 is supplied and protected by the line for fuse F05 located in the engine compartment junction unit B001.When the air conditioning is switched on the climate control system control unit M070 supplies the air conditioning/heater controls light G045. The same control unit receives an earth signal at pin 1.

Description The left button on the climate control system control unit switches on the air cooling and dehumidification circuit, activating the air conditioning compressor.The above button enables operation of the air cooling circuit, but actual compressor activation is also dependent upon activation of:the four-stage pressure switch located on the coolant circuit that locks air conditioner activation if coolant pressure is too low or high;the engine control unit that excludes compressor operation in accordance with engine management mode; e.g. in the case of high engine temperatures or high engine load (sudden acceleration);information from the antifrost thermostat about the presence or absence of condensation on the air conditioning system pipes.The compressor supply circuit is controlled by a special relay located in the engine bay junction unit. The relay supply line is protected by a special fuse.

Operational Description The compressor activation circuit is controlled by relay T05, contained in engine bay junction unit B001. This is supplied directly by a line from the battery that enters at pin 1 of control unit connector F and is protected by fuse F19, located in the control unit.During engine start-up, control unit M010 of connector A pin 13 excites relay T09 to provide it with an earth signal. The relay receives power directly from the battery protected by fuse F18. Relay T05 is supplied in turn and excited by engine control unit M010, connector A pin 18, when compressor activation is required.The compressor actiation request comes from climate control unit M070 - pin 4. The signal firstly reaches electronic thermostat N086 and then antifrost thermostat K160. Engine control unit M010 processes signal from both frost thermostats and multistage pressure switch K010. If the pressure and temperature readings from the air conditioning system are correct, the control unit excites relay T05 via pin 18 of connector A to supply compressor L020.Climate control unit M070 receives a power supply via the ignition and direct from the battery. The former is protected by fuse F31 hosed in underfacia junction unit B002 and the latter is protected by fuse F34 housed in optional junction unit B101. The climate control unit contains its own internal lighting that comes on when the side lights are on. When there is a request to switch on the compressor, the engine management control unit M010 supplies the relay coil T09 housed in the engine compartment junction unit B001 from pin F3 connector C; the relay is energized when control unit M010 sends an earth signal to pin A4 connector B. The supply from the relay T09 is direct from the battery and is supplied to relay T05 and relay J021.When energized, relay T05 supplies relay J020; the latter is operated by the engine management control unit M010 (pin D3 connector A). When energized, it closes its internal contact, supplying compressor L020.Relay J021 guarantees the connection to earth C040 for the relay coil J020 (pin 1). Pin 3 receives a supply from the line protected by fuse F17; when the control unit M010 sends an earth signal, from pin C3 connector A, the relay disconnects the earth at relay J020 and, as a result, the compressor L020 no longer receives a supply.

Description The basic air conditioner is complemented by a supplementary air conditioner to offer all passengers comfortable environmental conditions by taking in cool air even when temperature and relative humidity are high. The supplementary air condition is activated with the basic air conditioner by means of a specific button on the air conditioning system control panel. Special adjustable, positionable direct the air flow toward passengers in the central and rear seating rows. The supplementary air conditioner is activated automatically when the basic air conditioner is turned on. The power supplies are protected by special fuses in the engine bay junction unit, underfacia control unit and optional underfacia control unit.

Operational Description The supplementary air conditioner is activated by pressing a key located in climate control unit M070 - pin 4 -. Control unit M070 receives a power supply via the ignition and directly from the battery at pins 3 and 2. The ignition-operated power supply is protected by fuse F31, located in underfacia junction unit B002, and fuse F34, located in the optional underfacia junction unit B101. An activation control from pin 3 of control unit M070 reaches relays J132 and J121. Both relays are excited and supply battery power to switch H100. Relay J132 turns on the first speed automatically to supply fan N084 via resistor O031 - pins 1 and 3. For the second speed, the power supply flows through resistance load O030 - pins 2 and 3 -; while the power supply for the third speed is directed to motor N084 - pin 1 -. The direct battery power supply supplied to relays J121 and 132 is protected by fuse F56, located in optional junction unit B101. The following figure does not show electrical components belonging to the supplementary Air Conditioner wiring circuit.

Description To increase protection against theft attempts, an engine immobilizer system known as the FIAT CODE-2 is used. The keys are equipped with an electronic Transponder device that sends a coded signal to a special electronic CODE control unit. If the code transmitted is recognised as valid, the control unit allows the engine to be started. Because the code used in the communication - which takes place via aerial - changes at each start-up (rolling code), the code may not be reproduced even using electronic scanners. The CODE control unit and the engine management unit exchange information on the code received from the key inserted. If the code of the key in question is correct, the engine management control unit enables engine ignition. The entire system is protected by dedicated fuses housed in the engine bay and under-facia junction unit and a further maxifuse housed in the battery control unit.

Operational Description Ignition switch H001 is supplied via the ignition at pin 2 connector A. The line is protected by maxifuse F70 housed in battery control unit B099 and a further fuse F03 housed in engine bay control unit B001. When the ignition is turned ON, the power supply passes through a line protected by fuse F16 located in junction unit B001 to reach engine mangement unit M010, pin 58 (pin B4 connector A for 2.0 petrol versions). CODE control unit M020 receives a key inserted code via transponder P091 and checks its validity by comparing it with codes stored in its memory. If the code is correct CODE control unit M020 enables control unit M010 to start the engine as soon as required and simultaneously controls activation of the warning light on instrument panel E050 by earthing pin 2 of its own connector B.

Description The alarm system offers volume-sensing and perimeter protection against intrusion into the vehicle. A dedicated control unit monitors the following: the state of the doors and lids, via switches in the catches (perimeter control) the presence of a moving object inside the passenger compartment, by means of volume-sensing sensor (volumetric control) the condition of the system supply leads; operation of the ignition switch. The control unit is equipped with a self-diagnostic function which detects and memorises faults and problems in the control unit and system components; in addition, it checks the condition of the connecting cables and saves the number of activations and times the alarm has been operated. The control unit operating strategy can be modified in order to satisfy the legal requirements which govern the use of alarm systems in the various markets. The door lock system switches are used to monitor the doors and boot. A special separate switch detects bonnet closure. The volumetric sensors check for intrusions into the vehicle. They are located in the front courtesy light: they consist of a transmitter and a receiver: the wave transmitted by one transmitter must reach the receiver of the other sensor and viceversa: otherwise an alarm signal is sent to the control unit. The function may be activated/deactivated by pressing a key next to the sensors: when the sensors are excluded, a led next to the button is turned on System activation is displayed by means of a special deterrent led.

Operational Description The alarm system is fully managed by alarm control unit M030. The control unit receives an ignition-operated supply protected by fuse F27 - located in underfacia control unit B002 - and a direct battery supply protected by fuses F60 and F34 - located in optional junction unit B101 -. The control unit comprises two connectors, A and B, with the following pin-outs: Connector A: pin 1 : deterrent Led activation/deactivation; pin 3 : battery supply; pin 4 : system deactivation from remote key I100 - pin 1 connector B -; pin 7 : system activation from remote key I100 - pin 2 connector B -; pin 8 : volumetric sensor power supply K062 - pin 1 -; pin 9 : earth connection C010 - pin 10 -; pin 11 : earth reference for volumetric sensors K062 - pin 3 -; pin 12 : volumetric sensor power supply K062 - pin 2 -. Connector B: pin 1 : right turn signal power supply to control panel H090 - pin 7 connector A -; pin 2 : left turn signal power supply to control panel H090 - pin 5 connector A -; pin 7 : power supply direct from battery for controlling right and left turn signals; pin 8 : left front door open signal input from control panel H090 - pin 1 connector A -; pin 9 : right front door open signal input from control panel H090 - pin 1 connector A -; pin 12 : ignition-operated power supply; pin 13 : shared power supply for remote key I100 - pin 2 connector A -; pin 16 : right sliding door and door flaps open signal from control panel H090 - pin 6 connector A -; pin 18 : bonnet open signal input, from switch on bonnet I010 - pin 1 -; Remote control receiver M035 controls vehicle door catch closure/opening. More specifically, door unlocking is controlled from pin 5. The signal is distributed to the catches by short-circuiting junction D0971. Door locking is controlled from pin 6, distributed from short-circuiting junction D097G. Pin 3 receives a power supply directly from the battery while pin 7 receives an ignition-operated power supply.

Description The electronic antilock braking system regulates the braking pressure transmitted to the wheels, preventing them from losing grip whatever the tyre and road conditions. The system is designed to complement the conventional mechanical braking system and not to replace it, thereby guaranteeing effective safety in the case of problems: the system operates using the same brake fluid as in the conventional mechanical brake circuit. Four sensors, located on each of the four wheels, indicatae the speed of each wheel to the electronic control unit, recording any situations involving locking, slipping or loss of grip. If these situations occur, the electronic control unit operates solenoid valves, which modulate pressure in the hydraulic circuit to prevent lock and restore the vehicle to permissible grip limits to ensure the shortest possible stopping distance without losing control of the steering. Two regulation solenoids are fitted (a pressure charge solenoid and a pressure discharge solenoid) for each wheel. The sensors are active type, i.e. they consist of a receiver that faces a magnetic encoder built into in the hub bearing: under these conditions, the signal is less influenced by electromagnetic interferenced and temperature. In addition, the control unit manages distribution of the braking load over the rear axle to replace the mechanical load proportioning valve used previously (EBD function: Electronic Brake Distribution"). The control unit is equipped with an autodiagnostic function: when an error is detected in the ABS function, it turns on the associated warning light and simultaneously deactivates the system: under these conditions the vehicle is braked using only the conventional braking system. When the control unit detects an error in the EBD function, it turns on the low brake fluid and handbrake warning light together with the ABS failure warning light. Under these conditions, the rear brake distributor control is deactivated and the vehicle must be driven with great caution. The lines supplying the control unit and the various system components (sensors and actuators) are protected by dedicated by fuses located inside the engine bay control unit and the under-facia junction unit.

Operational Description ABS control unit M050 receives a power supply directly from the battery - pins 17 and 18 - and an ignition-operated supply - pin 15 -. The direct battery power supply is protected by fuse F04 located in engine bay junction unit B001. The ignition-operated supply is protected by fuse F42, located in the under-facia junction unit B002. When the brake pedal is pressed, switch I030 supplies control unit M070 - pin 14 - with an ignition-operated supply protected by fuse F26, located in control unit B002. ABS control unit M050 activates wheel sensors K070, K071, K075 and K076 via pins 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9. Control unit M070 communicates via the CAN with engine control unit M010, from pins 29 and 30. If the system malfunctions, the control unit turns on the warning lights located on instrument panel E050.

Description The electronic wheel anti-lock and anti-slip system regulations braking pressure transmitted to the wheels to prevent loss of grip under all tyre and road surface conditions and controls vehicle traction (ASR = ANTISLIP REGULATION) by cutting in automatically whenever one or both of the drive wheels begins to slip. The ASR system increases the active safety and stability of the vehicle controlling the slipping of the drive wheels: if slip is caused by the transmission of excessive power, the system cuts in, with the co-operation of the engine management control unit, to reduce engine power output. If, on the other hand, slip is detected at one wheel only, the system cuts in to brake only the slipping wheel by means of the wheel's modulating solenoid valve. The ASR comes on automatically whenever the engine is started: the system can be deactivated by means of a button on the control pane. With the system switched off, the warning light in the instrument panel comes on. The warning light flashes when the system cuts in to notifiy the driver that the ASR has come on due to road grip conditions. When the control unit detects an error in the ASR function, it turns on the warning light in fixed mode.

Operational Description ABS control unit M050 receives a power supply directly from the battery - pins 17 and 18 - and an ignition-operated supply - pin 15 -. The direct battery power supply is protected by fuse F04 located in engine bay junction unit B001. When the brake pedal is pressed, switch I030 supplies control unit M070 - pin 14 - with an ignition-operated supply protected by fuse F26, located in control unit B002. Description The vehicle is equipped with an electronically controlled safety system which, in the case of a frontal impact of a certain severity, activates the front Air Bags protecting the driver and the passenger.In the case of side impact of a certain severity, the front and rear Side Bags and a curtain-type Head Bag located on the front door pillar are activated.An electronic control unit manages the entire system controlling all the components and activating the Air Bag protection systems when necessary.An accelerometric sensor on the pillar of both front doors transmits a signal to the control unit in the case of a side impact.This signal is also processed inside the control unit, which may then decide to activate the Side Bags on the side where the impact was detected.The control unit is located in the middle of the facia and is secured rigidly to the body: in this way the deceleration sensors located inside the unit are near the centre of gravity and detect the deceleration for the entire vehicle accurately.The driver side air bag module is located in the middle of the steering wheel. It is fitted on a tilting plate that is also used to control the horns. The plate houses a metal container that contains the folded bag and the gas generation device that inflates the bag.A clock spring allows the connecting cables for the Air Bag module to follow the rotation of the steering wheel without danger of breaking.The passenger Air Bag module is located on the dashboard, and is fastened directly to the vehicle crossmember by means of a special bracket.The passenger air bag may be deactivated manually by means of a special switch on the facia.With the key OFF the control unit also controls activation of a special "passenger air bag disabled" warning light.The side bag is housed in the external part of the front seat. The associated sensor is located on the central pillar.The control unit is equipped with an autodiagnostic function:it detects and stores faultsit recognises the various components and the fault type;it indicates the onset of faults by means of warning lightsThe activation of the system following a particularly serious impact is memorized by the control unit.The air bag control unit power supply is protected by a fuse in the under-facia junction unit.The air bag system may come in several configurations (containing more or fewer components) according to the vehicle specification. None of the specifications includes a driver's side bag and a pretensioner for the front central passenger seat belt.

Operational Description Air Bag M060 consists of two connectgors, A and B, with the following pin-outs:Connector A:pin 1: connection to earth C050 connector A;pin 5: connection with Connect M120 front panel for vehicle speed signal;pin 6: connection to tester input;pin 7: control of passenger air bag deactivation warning light on instrument panel E050 - pin 17 connector E -: when pins 10 and 11 of control unit M060 receives an air bag deactivation control from switch H075, the unit turns on the relevant warning light by supplying it with power;pin 8: control of air bag failure warning light on instrument panel E050 - pin 8 connector B -: the warning light is ignition-operated by a line protected by fuse F37 - housed in under-facia control unit B002 - and is turned on only if control unit M060 supplies an earth signal;pins 10 and 11: connection to passenger air bag deactivation switch H075;pin 12: ignition-operated power supply protected by fuse F50 located in underfacia control unit B002;pin 17, 18: connection to passenger air bag (central) Q013;pin 21, 22: connection to passenger air bag (exteranl) Q012;pin 23, 24: connection to driver's air bag Q009.Connector B:pin 1, 2: connection to driver side front seat belt pretensioner Q020;pin 3, 4: connection to passenger side front seat belt pretensioner Q021;pin 5, 6: connection to central front seat belt pretensioner Q019 (if pretensioner fitted) or driver's side bag Q030 (if side bag fitted);pin 9, 10: connection to passenger side bag Q031;pin 17, 32: connection to earth C050 connector B;pin 24, 26: connection to sensor for driver's side bag, K066;pin 25, 27: connection to sensor for passenger side bag, K067.

Description The vehicle is equipped with automatic transmission which regulates and controls the automatic engagement of the gears.An electronic control unit manages a complex operating logic that allows the use of the gearbox in both sequential conditions, in which the driver manages the engagement of the gears using the lever and, in automatic mode, where the management of the gear changes is delegated to the electronic system.The automatic transmission control unit can move automatically to different programmes in relation to specific conditions, such as: driving up a hill, down a hill or round a bend, unmade roads, etc. and, on the basis of fundamental parameters such as the vehicle speed, engine speed and pressure on the brake pedal.Using the special signals transmitted by the automatic transmission control unit, the instrument panel matrix display shows device failure status and also warns of automatic transmission fluid overheating, whilst the milometer indicates the gear currently selected. There is also a buzzer if the gearbox is not in the safety "P" (Parking) position or if it is in the reverse position "R" withe the driver's door open.The control unit has its own diagnostic signal used for the continuous monitoring of the entire device.VedereE8010CONNETTORE MULTIPLO DI DIAGNOSIThe system is also controlled by a relay located in the engine compartment junction unit.The supply lines for the control units and the various system components are protected by special fuses in the engine bay and under-facia junction units.

Operational Description A direct supply from the battery is sent to gear selector H081 - pin E -, automatic transmission control unit M055 - pin 26 -, ignition switch electromagnet L057 - pin 2 - and multifunction selector H037 - pin 2 -. The line is protected by fuse F23, also located in engine bay junction unit B001.The ignition-operated power supply is supplied to gear selector H037 - pin 1 and automatic transmission control unit M055 - pins 54 and 55 -. The line is protected by fuse F24, also located in engine bay junction unit B001.Automatic transmission control unit M055 consists of a single connector with the following pin-out:the unit receives information on vehicle speed, rpm and transmission fluid temperature from pins 1, 4, 5, 14, 21, 22, 29, 30, 33, 52, 53, 16, 44 and controls solenoids that are built into the unit;pin 6, 28 and 34 supply earth reference C010 - pin 17 -;the unit supplies the vehicle speed signal to instrument panel E050 - pin 15 connector D from pin 27;the unit receives a gear shift command from multifunction switch I081 - pins A, B, C, D - from pins 9, 37, 8 and 36;the unit communicates with speed selector H037 - pins 5, 7 - via pins 82, 83-; at pin 88 the control unit is connected to the diagnostic socketVedereE8010CONNETTORE MULTIPLO DI DIAGNOSIit receives information on front driver door status (closed/open) at pin 19.Engine start-up is enabled on with speed selector I081 in parking position (P). In this situation, an earth connection is provided for relay coil T20. The relay coil is supplied with the key in AVV position (15/54) from a line protected by fuse F16, to supply starter motor A020.Speed selector H037 receives information on vehicle speed from instrument panel E050 - pin 2 connector C - and exchanges information on the CAN network with engine management controlo unit M010 - pins 9 and 10 of connector A -:The unit receives a signal from ignition switch electromagnet L057 at pin 9.The WINTER key on gear selector H037 is used to turn the ASR system on and off.

Description The car is fitted with numerous electronic control units that perform a self-diagnostic function.When a diagnostic tester (Examiner or other device) is connected to these control units, self-diagnosis data can be read (parameters, errors) or the available active diagnostic tests can be carried out.Each control unit converts its self-diagnostic line into a single connector that can be connected to the diagnostic tester.The following control units are connected to the diagnostic connector:alarm control unit;Air Bag control unit;engine management control unit;Fiat Code control unit;additional heater control unit;ABS control unit;Connect;alarm remote control receiver control unit;automatic transmission control unit;LPG control unit;methane injection control unit.

Operational Description The power supply to diagnostic joint R010 is supplied by control panel H090 - pin 4 connector B -.Power is supplied directly from the battery and protected by fuses F01 and F39 housed in engine bay junction unit B001 and the junction unit beneath the instrument facia B002.The junction pins are connected as follows:pins 4 and 5: connected to earth C015;pin 1: connected to ABS control unit M050, pin 48;pin 3: connected to air bag control unit M060, pin 6 connector A;pin 7: connection with the engine management control unit M010, pin 48 connector A (pin H2 connector A for 2.0 petrol versions) and with the automatic transmission control unit M055 (pin 88);pin 8: connected to Fiat Code control unit M020, pin 5 connector A;pin 9: connected to Connect M120, pin 2 connettore D;pin 11: connected to alarm control unit M030, pin 6, and alarm remote control receiver control unit M035, pin 2;pin 12: connected to additional heater control unit M075, pin C.pin 15: connection with LPG control unit M018 pin 15 connector A with the methane control unit M019 pin 15 connector A depending on the version of the vehicle.
